newsitem.title: CHINA: Lafarge invests $75 mln more in China.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge invests $75 mln more in China.

text.p: France's Lafarge will increase its stake in one of its joint ventures in China by investing an additional $75 million in a cement plant near Beijing, the company said on Thursday.
The new investment brings Lafarge's commitment in Beijing Chinefarge Cement Co and two other joint ventures in China to about $200 million, a company official said earlier.
The additional funds will boost production capacity to almost one million tonnes annually from 235,000 tonnes currently, the company said.
The new investment was announced after approval from China's State Planning Commission for the expansion and was timed to coincide with the visit of French President Jacques Chirac.

Lafarge holds a 51 percent stake Beijing Chinefarge, Citicorp holds 14 percent, the Huaibei Mining Co holds 20 percent and the State Develoment Industrial Corp holds 15 percent. The plant is in Huairou on the outskirts of Beijing.

"The Chinefarge expansion project will contribute to the development of the Beijing construction industry and demonstrates the commitment of Lafarge and our partners to providing the high quality building materials required by our customers in China," Lafarge president Bertrand Collomb said.
